text_blocks.snippet: Cirrhosis treatment focuses on managing symptoms, preventing complications, and slowing disease progression. While cirrhosis is generally irreversible, treatment can significantly improve quality of life and potentially extend lifespan. Treatment often involves addressing the underlying cause of liver disease, such as hepatitis or alcohol abuse, and managing complications like portal hypertension, ascites, and hepatic encephalopathy. In some cases, a liver transplant may be necessary.

Portal Hypertension: Medications like beta-blockers can help reduce pressure in the portal vein, reducing the risk of bleeding.
